rows.grounds: in the form of food as object of enjoyment
consisting of sound, touch, and taste

items.question: What is the supreme vital power of that seed described as?
premises: That seed also has a supreme vital power.
This vital power consists of the five elements.
As an object of enjoyment it appears as food.
It consists of sound, touch, and taste.
items.inference: The supreme vital power of the seed manifests as elemental food endowed with sound, touch, and taste.
items.plain_english: That seed too has a supreme vital power made of the five elements. As something to be enjoyed it takes the form of food, consisting of sound, touch, and taste.

rows.grounds: because it causes increase of vital power
whose nature is the desire to emit

items.question: Why is sound considered sweet and linked to supreme vital power?
premises: Sound is sweet because it increases vital power.
That vital power is supreme and pure.
That vital power is regarded as having the nature of a desire to emit.
items.inference: Sweet sound nourishes the supreme pure vital power whose essence is the impulse to emanate.
items.plain_english: Sound too is sweet because it increases vital power. That vital power is supreme and pure, and it is understood to have the nature of a desire to emit.

rows.grounds: from that vital power come offspring and

items.question: How does vital power manifest in beings and in ritual action?
premises: Vital power appears as strength, vigor, the vital breaths, and loveliness.
From that vital power offspring arise.
Vital power is spoken of in ritual acts.
items.inference: The same vital power expresses itself as bodily excellence, procreation, and efficacy in ritual.
items.plain_english: That vital power is strength, vigor, the vital breaths, and loveliness. From it offspring arise, and it is also spoken of in ritual acts.

rows.grounds: the state of having all forms

items.question: How does emission display universal formhood through its cycle?
premises: Vital power operates in sacrifice and other rites.
It appears in rain, then in plants, then again in vital power, and then in offspring.
This circulation occurs within emission.
items.inference: Emission reveals universal formhood by circulating as the same vital power through ritual, nature, and progeny.
items.plain_english: In sacrifice and other rites, in rain, in plants, again in vital power, and then in offspring, the same power circulates. Thus emission takes on the form of the whole universe.

rows.grounds: from entering the state of being agitated and agitating, Malini

items.question: How is the totality of sound identified as Matrika and Malini?
premises: The totality of sound is called Matrika.
Matrika is proclaimed as Malini.
This name arises from entering the state of being both agitated and agitating.
items.inference: The same sonic totality is Matrika in essence and Malini in its dynamic, stirring aspect.
items.plain_english: That whole mass of sound is called Matrika. Because it enters a state of being both stirred and stirring, it is also declared to be Malini.

rows.grounds: beautiful through the union of seed and womb and the arising of emission
is determined to be the power
having the form of the universe

items.question: What is Malini determined to be in her supreme nature?
premises: Malini is beautiful through the union of seed and womb and the arising of emission.
She is determined to be the supreme power.
She has the form of the universe.
items.inference: Malini is the supreme cosmic power whose creative emission manifests as the universe.
items.plain_english: Malini, beautiful through the union of seed and womb and the rise of emission, is indeed determined to be the supreme power that takes the form of the whole universe.

rows.grounds: through connection with the differentiation of the power-holder
the state of being a pair

items.question: How does the one supreme power come to appear as a pair?
premises: This supreme power is in reality one alone.
She draws forth time.
Through connection with the differentiation of the power-holder she attains the state of being a pair.
items.inference: The single supreme power appears as a dyad through its relation to the differentiated power-holder.
items.plain_english: In reality this supreme power is one alone and draws forth time. Yet through its connection with the differentiation of the power-holder, it takes on the form of a pair.

rows.grounds: whose nature is the perfect I
because of freedom would manifest division
rows.morph: 3.sg.optative, root bhās with ava, compound svatantratvāt-vibhāgam-avabhāsayet

items.question: What does the perfect reflective awareness do within itself?
premises: There is a reflective awareness whose nature is the perfect I.
That awareness abides in its own self.
Because of its freedom it can manifest division within itself.
items.inference: The perfect I, by its own freedom, manifests division within its undivided self-awareness.
items.plain_english: That reflective awareness, whose nature is the perfect I, abides in its own self and, by its freedom, manifests division within itself.

items.question: How is the body of awareness described when division appears?
premises: When division is manifested, the body of this awareness is declared threefold.
The three forms are Pashyanti, Madhyama, and the gross Vaikhari.
items.inference: The manifestation of division unfolds as the three levels of speech: Pashyanti, Madhyama, and Vaikhari.
items.plain_english: When division appears, this awareness is said to take a threefold body: Pashyanti, Madhyama, and the gross level called Vaikhari.

rows.grounds: according to gross, subtle, and supreme
beautiful with a flow of tones

items.question: How are the three levels of speech further subdivided?
premises: Each of those three levels also has a threefold form.
The subdivision is according to gross, subtle, and supreme.
Among them is a form beautiful with flowing tones and having the nature of sound.
items.inference: The three speech levels are internally differentiated, and one of their forms is the tonal, sound-like nada.
items.plain_english: Each of those three also has a threefold form: gross, subtle, and supreme. Among them is a form beautiful with flowing tones, having the nature of sound.

rows.grounds: because letters and so on are not yet divided
the state of being a single undivided form

items.question: What characterizes the gross aspect of Pashyanti?
premises: The gross aspect is Pashyanti.
In it letters and other divisions have not yet appeared.
Its undivided single form is called sweetness and power.
items.inference: Gross Pashyanti is an undivided sonic power experienced as sweetness before phonemic articulation.
items.plain_english: That gross aspect is indeed Pashyanti. Since letters and other divisions have not yet appeared there, its single undivided form is called sweetness and power.

rows.grounds: arising from friction of articulatory place, breath, and so on
from functioning in proximity to consciousness

items.question: How do clearness and harshness arise in relation to nada?
premises: Harshness and clearness arise from friction of articulatory place, breath, and other factors.
In this sound-form, functioning occurs near consciousness.
items.inference: Articulatory friction produces harsh clearness, but in nada it is still experienced close to pure consciousness.
items.plain_english: Clearness and harshness arise from the friction of articulatory place, breath, and so on. Yet in this sound-form they function in close proximity to consciousness.

rows.morph: 3.sg.passive-present, root labh with upa, compound yībhūtiḥ-jhagiti-eva-upalabhyate

rows.grounds: immersion in body and so on

items.question: What happens to those who do or do not become absorbed in nada?
premises: Inner absorption in sameness with that sound is perceived suddenly.
Some do not attain absorption into that state.
Those who do not attain it remain immersed in body and related limitations.
items.inference: Sudden identification with nada lifts awareness, while failure to identify leaves one sunk in bodily consciousness.
uncertainties: The bracketed reading antarma[ttama] is uncertain in the supplied text.
items.plain_english: Absorption into that same sound is perceived suddenly. Those who do not become absorbed in it remain sunk in the body and similar limitations.

rows.grounds: but with the measure of consciousness sunk and not centered in the heart
whatever comes from a skin-covered drum and so on

items.question: How is ordinary resonant sound related to unabsorbed awareness?
premises: Those not knowing remain with consciousness sunk and not centered in the heart.
A sound arises from things like a skin-covered drum.
That sound is present there as an object of perception.
items.inference: For unabsorbed awareness, sound is encountered only as an external resonance rather than as inwardly recognized nada.
items.plain_english: Those who do not know remain with their awareness sunk and not centered in the heart. For them, the sound that comes from a skin-covered drum or the like is just an external resonance.

rows.grounds: because of being clear and unclear, Madhyama
and of Madhyama the presence of an undivided aspect

items.question: What defines the gross form of Madhyama speech?
premises: Madhyama is characterized by being both clear and unclear.
Its gross form is identified accordingly.
Madhyama also contains an undivided aspect, described as coloration.
items.inference: Gross Madhyama stands between undivided sound and clear articulation, retaining a subtle coloring of unity.
items.plain_english: Because it is both clear and unclear, that gross form is Madhyama. Madhyama also contains an undivided aspect, which is described as its coloration.

items.question: Why is undivided tonal sound experienced as delightful?
premises: A form made of undivided tones is delighting.
Non-division brings fulfillment.
This can be observed in the recitation of rhythm.
items.inference: Undivided tonal continuity delights because it restores a sense of wholeness, as heard in rhythmic recitation.
items.plain_english: Where sound is made of undivided tones, it is delighting. Non-division brings fulfillment, as can be seen in the recitation of rhythm.

items.question: What role does unmanifest sound play relative to articulated letters?
premises: One is satisfied in that unmanifest sound during musical playing.
There is a principle that would be the cause of the arising of clear letters.
items.inference: Unmanifest sound is both intrinsically satisfying and the causal ground for articulated phonemes.
items.plain_english: One feels satisfied in that unmanifest sound during musical playing. Yet that same level can also serve as the cause for the arising of clear letters.

rows.grounds: that connecting awareness like the first

items.question: What is the function of gross Vaikhari within the gross triad?
premises: The gross level is Vaikhari.
Its function is chiefly sentences and other articulated speech.
Within the gross triad there is a connecting awareness like the first.
items.inference: Gross Vaikhari produces articulated speech while still participating in a unifying awareness across the triad.
items.plain_english: That gross level is Vaikhari, whose function is mainly sentences and other articulated speech. Even within this gross triad there is a connecting awareness like the first.

items.question: How is the subtle triad illustrated in lived experience?
premises: When the triad is taken separately, it is called subtle.
Examples include intending a note, playing sweetly, and speaking words.
items.inference: The subtle triad appears as distinct inner operations behind musical intention, performance, and speech.
items.plain_english: When that triad is taken separately, it is called subtle. It is seen in experiences like 'I make the note shadja,' 'I play sweetly,' and 'I speak words.'

rows.grounds: which form is without limiting condition

items.question: What is the highest aspect within the subtle triad of awareness?
premises: A threefold connecting awareness is experienced separately.
Within that triad there is a first aspect.
That first aspect is without limiting condition.
items.inference: Even in differentiated awareness, the first term of the triad points to an unconditioned ground.
items.plain_english: A threefold connecting awareness is indeed experienced separately. Of that triad, the first aspect is a form without limiting condition.

items.question: What stands at the supreme level behind the triad of manifestation?
premises: That triad is supreme.
There Shiva is of the nature of supreme consciousness.
In the manifestation of division three principal powers appear.
items.inference: Supreme consciousness as Shiva manifests division through three principal powers.
items.plain_english: That is the supreme triad. There Shiva is of the nature of supreme consciousness, and in the manifestation of division three principal powers appear.

rows.grounds: the power of unfolding called knowledge

items.question: Which three principal powers are identified at the supreme level?
premises: Anuttara is present as supreme will.
Another power stands as supreme-and-non-supreme.
The unfolding power called knowledge is declared as the lower.
items.inference: The three principal powers are will, an intermediate power, and knowledge as unfolding.
items.plain_english: The three principal powers are Anuttara as supreme will, the power situated as supreme-and-non-supreme, and the unfolding power called knowledge, which is declared as the lower.

rows.grounds: again from their stirring form are declared
from immersion arisen as the power of action

items.question: How do the three powers further differentiate into six cognitions?
premises: From the stirring form of those powers, six immaculate cognitions are declared.
These arise from the immersion of those same powers.
That immersion is expressed as the power of action.
items.inference: The three powers, stirred into action, differentiate into six immaculate modes of cognition.
items.plain_english: From the stirring of those powers, six immaculate cognitions are declared. They arise from the immersion of those same powers as the power of action.

rows.grounds: this much of the God of gods

items.question: What is the principal wheel of powers of the God of gods?
premises: Twelve cognitions are declared.
In them all is contained.
This constitutes the principal wheel of powers of the God of gods.
items.inference: The twelve cognitions form the chief power-wheel in which the whole manifestation is gathered.
items.plain_english: Twelve cognitions are declared, and in them all is contained. This is the principal wheel of powers of the God of gods.
